## 2026-07-24 06:43 · base 0dc0b749202c

This session hardens the digest format against a live-demo bug where LLM-generated narratives containing `##` headings broke `upsert_digest`'s entry-boundary detection, causing phantom entries and failed same-base replacements. The fix is applied at three independent layers: stricter parsing in `upsert_digest`, heading demotion in `render_digest_section`, and a prompt-level instruction in `_NARRATIVE_SYSTEM_PROMPT`.

### Entry-boundary parsing (`upsert_digest`)

The core bug was that entry splitting matched any line starting with `## `, so a narrative containing `## Some Section` would be mis-parsed as a new entry boundary.

- `upsert_digest` now uses a strict regex — `^## \d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}.* · base [0-9a-fA-F]+` — that matches only lines with the canonical entry-heading shape. Bare `##` lines anywhere inside a narrative body are invisible to the splitter.
- Same-base replace and `max_entries` trim semantics are unchanged.

### Heading demotion in rendered output (`render_digest_section`)

Even with correct parsing, an H1 or H2 inside a rendered entry breaks the document's visual hierarchy.

- `render_digest_section` now post-processes the narrative line-by-line before embedding it: any line starting with `# ` or `## ` has its leading hashes replaced with `### `.
- The pass is fence-aware: a running `in_fence` flag toggled on `` ``` `` lines ensures diff blocks and code samples are never mangled.
- The triefact description for `render_digest_section` was updated to reflect that it is now responsible for this demotion step.

### Prompt instruction (`_NARRATIVE_SYSTEM_PROMPT`)

As the cheapest preventive layer, the system prompt now explicitly instructs the LLM to use `###` or deeper for any sub-headings in its output, never `#` or `##`, because the narrative will be embedded beneath an `##` entry heading. The `_NARRATIVE_SYSTEM_PROMPT` triefact description was updated to document this constraint, and `synthesize_narrative`'s description was updated to note that it inherits the prompt change automatically.

### Tests

- `test_render_digest_section_shape` was extended to pass a narrative containing an `## Summary` heading and a fenced block with `## not a heading`, then assert: the rendered output contains `### Summary` (demoted), no bare `## Summary` outside fences, and the fenced line survives verbatim. A follow-up fix made the H2-scanning assertion itself fence-aware so it does not incorrectly flag the fenced line.
- `test_upsert_digest_prepend_replace_trim` was extended with a regression case: an entry whose narrative body contains `## Inner heading that is narrative, not an entry` is upserted, then replaced via same-base. The test asserts the inner `##` line did not create a phantom entry, the old body is gone, the replacement appears exactly once, and other entries are intact.

### Intent

- Fix the digest entry-boundary bug the live demo caught: LLM narratives legally contain ## headings, which upsert_digest mis-parsed as entry boundaries (phantom entries, broken same-base replace). Three layers: strict entry-heading regex in upsert_digest, heading demotion (fence-aware) in render_digest_section, and a prompt instruction to keep narrative headings at ### or deeper.

Assert the rendered output contains '### Summary' (demoted), does NOT contain a line '## Summary', and the fenced '## not a heading' line survives unmodified inside the fence. ### TRIE_DIFF digest system: pre-commit hook wiring, CLI `--write` flag, and digest helpers

This session added a complete `trie diff --write` digest pipeline — a prepend-only, newest-first `TRIE_DIFF.md` that every commit carries as a pure-addition diff — and fixed a batch of bugs and test defects that emerged during implementation. All changes are fully applied; nothing remains pending.

---

### Configuration (`trie/config`)

- **`Diff` dataclass** — new frozen-style config section with `narrative: bool = True`, `write_path: str = "TRIE_DIFF.md"`, and `max_entries: int = 20`; docstring explains the prepend-only PR-diff-cleanliness guarantee.
- **`Config`** — gains `diff: Diff = field(default_factory=Diff)` and corresponding `Config.from_dict` wiring.
- **`DEFAULT_CONFIG_TOML`** — commented `[diff]` block added for discoverability alongside other optional sections.

---

### Git helpers (`trie/git_helpers`)

- **`commit_timestamp(repo_root, ref="HEAD") -> float | None`** — new function; runs `git show -s --format=%ct <ref>` via `_run_git`, decodes bytes, parses as float, returns `None` on any failure.
- **Bug fix**: initial implementation assumed `_run_git` returns a `CompletedProcess`; corrected to decode the raw bytes directly (`result.decode(...).strip()`).

---

### Session diff helpers (`trie/session_diff`)

- **`collect_session_diff`** — gains `since: float | None = None` keyword parameter, forwarded to `read_entries`, so digest entries are scoped to notes recorded after the base commit.
- **`_diff_stat(diff_text) -> list[tuple[str, int, int]]`** — new private helper; parses unified git diff into per-file `(path, added, removed)` tuples without I/O.
- **`render_digest_section(data, *, base_short, date_str, narrative=""") -> str`** — new deterministic renderer producing one markdown digest entry: heading, optional narrative paragraph, `### Intent`, `### Applied`, `### Pending (staged, not applied)`, and `### Triefact changes` sections.
- **Bug fix**: initial implementation used attribute access on `applied`/`pending` entries that are plain dicts throughout the module; replaced all with `.get()` calls matching `build_narrative_prompt`.
- **`DIGEST_HEADER` constant** and **`upsert_digest(existing_text, section, *, base_short, max_entries=20) -> str`** — pure text transform implementing prepend-only semantics: replaces the top entry when `base_short` matches (amend/retry safety), otherwise prepends, then trims to `max_entries`. The header preamble is rewritten on every call so it self-heals across version changes.

---

### CLI (`trie/cli`)

- **`diff_cmd`** — gains `--write` boolean option. When set: computes `since` via `commit_timestamp`, skips on empty diff, resolves `base_short` from `current_head`, optionally calls `synthesize_narrative` (silently degrading to `narrative=""` on any exception including missing API key), then writes the upserted digest to `config.diff.write_path`. Never blocks a commit.

---

### Pre-commit hook (`trie/init`)

- **`PRE_COMMIT_HOOK_BLOCK`** — extended with an advisory digest refresh step inside the existing `command -v trie` guard, after `trie -q verify`:
  ```sh
  if trie -q diff --write >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      git add TRIE_DIFF.md >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
  ```
  Failure is explicitly non-blocking. Module-level comment updated with a numbered point 3 explaining the design and the hardcoded-filename caveat.

---

### Tests

**New tests:**
- **`test_commit_timestamp_returns_head_time`** — verifies HEAD returns a recent float, explicit `"HEAD"` matches it, a bad ref returns `None`, and a directory outside any repo returns `None`. Bug fix applied: repo is initialised in a `repo/` subdirectory of `tmp_path` so the "not a repo" sibling probe is genuinely outside any git work tree.
- **`test_hook_block_includes_diff_write`** — asserts `trie -q diff --write` and `git add TRIE_DIFF.md` are present, the digest step appears after `trie -q verify` (index comparison), and the diff-write line contains no `|| exit`.
- **`test_collect_session_diff_since_filters_applied`** — uses explicit `ts=100.0` / `ts=200.0` entries (avoiding wall-clock flakiness) and `since=150.0` to assert only the later entry is returned; `since=None` returns both. Bug fix: `from trie.store import Store` corrected to rely on the module-level `from trie.graph.store import Store`.
- **`test_render_digest_section_shape`** — verifies heading, narrative, all evidence subsections, per-file stat format, and that omitting `narrative` leaves the paragraph absent.
- **`test_upsert_digest_prepend_replace_trim`** — covers fresh file, prepend ordering, same-`base_short` replacement, and `max_entries` trimming as a pure text-transform test.

**Fixed existing tests:**

### Intent

- TRIE_DIFF.md digest system: `trie diff --write` maintains a prepend-only, newest-first intent digest at the repo root (LLM narrative by default per new [diff] config, deterministic evidence fallback), wired into the standard pre-commit hook as an advisory step after verify — so every commit and PR carries the latest session digest as a pure-addition diff, with applied notes scoped to the base commit via session-log timestamps.
- Fix two generation bugs in the digest system: commit_timestamp assumed _run_git returns a CompletedProcess (it returns stdout bytes), and render_digest_section used attribute access on applied/pending entries that are plain dicts.
- Fix three test defects introduced with the digest system: read_entries stub missing the session_id kwarg (and str-vs-float since, unittest.mock instead of pytest-mock), a wrong trie.store import path, and a not-a-repo probe that lived inside the test repo's work tree.

Returns the section text ending with a single trailing newline. No LLM calls here — narrative is passed in by the caller. (reason: Deterministic renderer for one commit's digest entry.)
- [create] trie/session_diff:upsert_digest — New function upsert_digest(existing_text: str, section: str, *, base_short: str, max_entries: int = 20) -> str. Maintains the prepend-only TRIE_DIFF.md digest:

1. Module-level constant DIGEST_HEADER (define it just above this function) containing the file preamble:
   `# TRIE_DIFF` title, then an HTML comment block explaining: auto-generated by `trie diff --write` (wired into the pre-commit hook); prepend-only, newest entry first; do not edit by hand; entries roll off after max_entries.
2. Split existing_text into entries: everything from each line matching regex ^## (multiline) to the next such line. Ignore any preamble before the first entry (it gets replaced by the canonical DIGEST_HEADER on every write, so header evolution is self-healing).
3. If the first (newest) existing entry's heading contains `base {base_short}` for the same base_short, REPLACE that entry with the new section (covers amend/retry of the same commit — no duplicate entries). Otherwise PREPEND the new section.
4. Truncate to at most max_entries entries.
5. Return DIGEST_HEADER + '\n' + entries joined with '\n' (normalise so entries are separated by exactly one blank line).

Pure text transform, no I/O — trivially testable. Handles existing_text='' (fresh file). (reason: Core of the prepend-only design: PR diffs of TRIE_DIFF.md are pure additions (plus clean roll-off deletions), never diff-of-a-diff noise.)

- [modify] tests/test_git_helpers:test_commit_timestamp_returns_head_time — Fix the not-a-repo probe: `not_a_repo` is currently created INSIDE tmp_path, which was git-inited, so it is inside the work tree and `git show` succeeds. Restructure: create the git repo in a subdirectory `repo = tmp_path / 'repo'; repo.mkdir()` (git init there, config, README, commit, and all commit_timestamp positive/missing-ref assertions run against `repo`), and keep `not_a_repo = tmp_path / 'not_a_repo'` — now genuinely outside any work tree since tmp_path itself is not a repo — asserting commit_timestamp(not_a_repo) is None. (reason: Assertion failure: subdir of the test repo is still inside the work tree, so the None probe never triggers.)
- [modify] tests/test_session_diff:test_collect_session_diff_gathers_all_evidence — Fix the since-forwarding block at the end of the test (it currently fails with TypeError):
1. The stub must accept the full keyword surface collect_session_diff uses: `def capturing_read_entries(project_root, *, session_id=None, since=None):` and forward both kwargs to original_read_entries.
2. `future_ts` must be a FLOAT unix timestamp (`time.time() + 3600`), not an ISO string — read_entries compares floats. Import time at the top of the block instead of datetime.
3. Repo convention (AGENTS.md): use the pytest-mock `mocker` fixture, not unittest.mock — add `mocker` to the test's parameters and replace the `with mock_patch.object(...)` context with `mocker.patch.object(_session_log, 'read_entries', side_effect=capturing_read_entries)` followed by the collect_session_diff call (mocker auto-undoes at test end).
Keep the assertions (captured_since == [future_ts], data_since.applied == []) and everything before the block unchanged. (reason: Stub signature omits session_id kwarg (TypeError), future_ts is a str compared against float ts, and unittest.mock violates the pytest-mock convention.)
- [modify] tests/test_session_diff:test_collect_session_diff_since_filters_applied — Fix the import: `from trie.store import Store` is wrong — the module is `trie.graph.store` (the file already imports it at top level, so simplest is to drop the local Store import entirely and rely on the module-level `from trie.graph.store import Store`). Keep the rest of the test unchanged. (reason: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'trie.store'.)
- [modify] tests/test_session_diff:test_collect_session_diff_since_filters_applied — Deflake: don't derive timestamps from wall-clock writes — the two record_applied calls can land in the same clock tick, making the midpoint filter nondeterministic (observed failure: both entries share a ts, midpoint excludes both). record_applied honours a caller-provided ts (`if not row.get("ts")`), so pass explicit timestamps: early entry {"ts": 100.0, ...}, late entry {"ts": 200.0, ...}, drop the read_entries timestamp discovery (keep the len==2 sanity assert if desired), and filter with since=150.0. Assertions unchanged: filtered contains pkg.late only; since=None contains both. (reason: Test is timing-flaky; explicit ts values make the since-filter spec deterministic.)
